bio.short: English novelist known for novels about the British landed gentry.
bio.long: Jane Austen was an English novelist whose works critique and comment upon the British landed gentry at the end of the 18th century. Her most famous novels include Pride and Prejudice, Sense and Sensibility, and Emma, celebrated for their wit, social commentary, and masterful character development.

bio.short: British author of novels, comics, and screen work.
bio.long: Neil Gaiman is a British author whose work crosses novels, comics, and film. He wrote American Gods on his own and Good Omens with Terry Pratchett.

bio.short: British novelist best known for the Discworld series.
bio.long: Terry Pratchett was a British author of comic fantasy. The Colour of Magic began the Discworld series. He co-wrote Good Omens with Neil Gaiman.

bio.short: American author best known for his highly influential dystopian novel Fahrenheit 451.
bio.long: Ray Bradbury was an American fantasy, science fiction, horror, and dystopian writer. He is celebrated for his 1953 masterpiece Fahrenheit 451, which explores a future society where books are outlawed and burned.

bio.short: American novelist and short story writer widely regarded as one of the greatest twentieth-century authors.
bio.long: F. Scott Fitzgerald was a prominent American. He is best known for his 1925 novel The Great Gatsby, a critique of the American Dream and the disillusionment of the roaring twenties.
